title: `npm run dev` cannot run on a clean shell: ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY is hard-required by DeployMocks but is set nowhere in the repository, and the .env.example the docs describe does not exist
severityRationale: Fails loudly and immediately, naming the exact variable, so it is discoverable rather than silent — that caps it well below the false-assurance channel. But it breaks the sole developer entry point for anyone who does not already have the variable in their ambient environment, which is an onboarding stop, not merely an annoyance.
description: DeployMocks.s.sol:419 reads `vm.envUint("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY")`. Neither dev-local.sh, package.json, nor any tracked file in the repository sets or exports it; `git ls-files | grep -i env` returns nothing and there is no .envrc, .env or .env.example in the source tree. Its only in-repo occurrence is a literal inside CLAUDE.md:476, in a block headed 'Required Variables in `.env`' — a file the repo neither ships nor ships an example of, even though CLAUDE.md:93-94 lists `.env.example` in its own directory-layout diagram and CLAUDE.md:454 instructs the reader to 'Create `.envrc.example`'. The same variable is read by script/interactions/StakeStableStaker.s.sol:37 and ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:40, so `npm run test:stable-staker` inherits the dependency.
failureScenario: A new developer clones phoenix-phase-2-staging, runs `npm install`, and follows the documented entry point with `npm run dev`. The port pre-flight passes, clean:local runs and deletes two tracked files, anvil starts and all four shell gates pass — and then the forge leg reverts at DeployMocks.s.sol:419 with 'environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found'. There is no .env.example in the tree to copy, so the only path to the value is finding the literal buried at CLAUDE.md:476. The developer is left with no dev stack and a working tree in which broadcast/DeployMocks.s.sol/31337/run-latest.json and server/deployments/progress.31337.json are now deleted.
impact: A developer cloning the repo and running the documented entry point gets a revert rather than a dev stack. This audit's own happy-path run only succeeded because direnv had already exported the variable from an out-of-repo .envrc; re-running with `env -u ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY` reproduced the failure.
evidence:
Ran: `cd <project>/work && env -u ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY ./dev-local.sh` -> EXIT=1.
Trace excerpt:
  [4141] DeployMocks::run()
    |- [0] VM::envUint("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY") [staticcall]
    |   |- <- [Revert] vm.envUint: environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found
  Error: script failed: vm.envUint: environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found
Provenance of the value in the passing run: `/home/justin/code/audits/.envrc` line 18 plus a byte-identical gitignored copy at `<project>/work/.envrc` (`git check-ignore -v .envrc` -> `.gitignore:6:.envrc`). `ls -a <project>/src | grep -i env` -> no match.
recommendation: Either default it in the script — `vm.envOr("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY", uint256(0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80))`, which is safe precisely because DeployMocks.s.sol:443 already requires chainid 31337 and the key is anvil's publicly-known account 0 — or export it in dev-local.sh next to the existing `LOCAL_PROMO_KENDU=true`. Whichever is chosen, commit the `.env.example` / `.envrc.example` that CLAUDE.md:93 and :454 already promise, so the dependency is discoverable before the revert.

dedup.reasoning: Same contract (script/DeployMocks.s.sol), same function (run), same entryPoint (dev), same defect: ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY is hard-required by vm.envUint and is not provided by the entry point. Q-02 already owns this. The new claim is a SHARPENING of the same root cause, not a second one: verified independently this run that the identifier appears in the tree only at CLAUDE.md:476 (prose) and in seven vm.envUint call sites, with no .env, no .env.example and no shell export anywhere, so `npm run dev` cannot complete on a clean shell. That escalates the CONSEQUENCE (entry point unrunnable, not merely undocumented) and warrants qa -> low on the EXISTING entry. Minting UndeclaredAmbientEnvDependency would re-hash contract:function:rootCauseClass:entryPoint into a second fingerprint for one defect and orphan Q-02's history - the ledger rootCauseClass mislabel trap. The rootCauseClass string is therefore left VERBATIM as UndocumentedRequiredEnvVar; only a human /ledger action may change it, and doing so re-mints the fingerprint.

classification.assetImpact: None. Onboarding/availability of the developer entry point only.
attackPath: No attacker. Reproduced as side-effects test B (`env -u ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY ./dev-local.sh`):
1. A developer clones the repo, `npm install`, `npm run dev` on a clean shell.
2. Pre-flight, clean:local, anvil start and all four shell gates PASS.
3. The forge leg reverts at DeployMocks.s.sol:419: environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found.
4. No .env.example exists to copy; the only in-repo occurrence of the value is prose at CLAUDE.md:476.
5. The developer is left with no stack AND a dirty tree - clean:local already deleted two TRACKED files that a failed run never re-creates.
classification.likelihood: certain for any developer without the variable already in their ambient environment. This audit's own happy-path run only succeeded because direnv had exported it from an OUT-OF-REPO .envrc.
classification.externalRequirements: None - it is the default state of a clean clone.

classifierJustification: CONFIRMED Low, and I ENDORSE the proposed qa->low escalation on existing entry d3aa1e35c995. It fails loudly and names the exact variable, so there is no false-assurance channel at all - that correctly caps it well below Medium. But it is more than documentation QA for two reasons: (1) it breaks the SOLE documented developer entry point on a clean clone, which is an availability stop on the harness rather than an annoyance; (2) the failure is not clean - clean:local has already deleted two git-TRACKED files by the time the revert lands, so the developer's first experience is a dirty tree plus no stack. That combination is exactly the 'state handling / incorrect as to spec' Low band, above pure informational QA.
caveatsForHuman: The escalation is PROPOSED ONLY and must be applied by a human via /ledger. This finding is an UPDATE to existing open entry d3aa1e35c995 (Q-02), not a new entry - do not insert.
